source.title: Ghost mechanism: An analytical model of abrupt learning in recurrent networks
source.authors: Fatih Dinç; Ege Çirakman; Bariscan Kurtkaya; Mert Yuksekgonul; Yi-Qi Jiang; Mark J. Schnitzer; Hidenori Tanaka

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no relevant truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training dynamics in canonical, low-rank, and full-rank RNNs and finds both abrupt learning and recurring failures: critical learning rates, oscillatory minima, and no-learning zones. It refines the broad training-success claim for recurrent working-memory tasks rather than CIFAR classification.
record.gate_note: The paper reports relevant training outcomes on delayed activation and working-memory tasks. Results about ghost points, speed minima, and trajectories are included only when tied to training loss, gradient, or accuracy outcomes. Cited feedforward results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests ghost-based learning in recurrent networks and a scalar dynamical model, but none of V1–V6. Critical learning rates are not measured relative to an initial linearized stability limit, and neither curvature reduction nor edge-of-stability sharpness is measured. Rank sweeps do not test two-layer ReLU teacher–student width effects. Xavier initialization is used as a recipe without testing its optimization benefit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors explain one mechanism of abrupt learning and associated failures through ghost dynamics, demonstrate related signatures in low-rank and full-rank RNNs, and find partial stabilization through additional trainable ranks and reduced output confidence. They acknowledge limited mechanistic interpretability in full-rank networks.
record.recipe_differences: The tested systems are continuous-time recurrent networks and a one-dimensional canonical dynamical model trained on delayed activation and working-memory tasks. The cited CIFAR and feedforward classification recipes are not tested.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with learning rate, trainable rank, task, delay duration, and output confidence. Rank-one and full-rank networks have different critical learning rates; increasing rank improves but does not eliminate instability. Lowering confidence can enable recovery, while excessively low confidence prevents sustained learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Ghost-based delayed-activation and working-memory learning exhibits abrupt loss drops, oscillatory gradients, and critical learning rates beyond which networks can enter no-learning zones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent temporal computations can impose optimization failures through ghost-based dynamics and confidently incorrect outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing trainable recurrent rank speeds learning and raises tolerable learning rates, while leaving some failures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional trainable recurrent ranks can partially stabilize ghost-based learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing output confidence restores gradients and can enable recovery, while excessively low confidence impairs performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-confidence interventions can mitigate recurrent no-learning zones within a useful confidence range.

record.problems: Most reported demonstrations are on recurrent working-memory tasks rather than classification. Several claims are illustrated by representative runs or figures; some sweeps report means and s.e.m. over ten seeds, while other rank sweeps show single runs per seed. Full-rank dynamical minima are found with a numerical solver initialized from observed trajectories. The paper itself notes full-rank mechanisms are harder to disentangle and its mechanistic picture is more limited there.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 convolutional training error, random or corrupted labels, and effects of size, stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher–student spurious minima and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks and prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal or gradient preservation across depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian training.
Recovery above an initial linearized stability limit, accompanying curvature reduction, edge-of-stability sharpness, and divergence despite initialization below that threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 designation overextends the listed claims. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because none measures their specified effects; this does not negate the recurrent-task findings. The paper's comparison to the catapult mechanism is an analogy, not a test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random labels, or comparison of model sizes and regularization is tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or teacher/student width sweep is tested.
No plain-versus-residual convolutional network depth comparison is tested.
No activation-matched initialization comparison or very deep plain feedforward network training is tested. RNN initializations are specified but not systematically compared.

The paper studies critical learning rates in recurrent networks, but does not test squared-loss wide-network catapult recovery, sharpness at the stability threshold, or the stated full-batch feedforward results.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup residual-network experiment is tested.

rows.subject: canonical model
rows.size_stated: one state variable and one parameter
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on the delayed-activation task, initialized at r = 10r*
rows.value: Loss decrease is abrupt around epoch 1500; lower learning rates with more epochs give lower final errors.
rows.note: The task is delayed activation, not classification. Text states the loss drops abruptly, while also noting training does not undergo a bifurcation at α = 10^-10.
rows.check: Delayed-activation loss does not measure any listed version. For the ten-instance experiment, initialization is distributed around 10r*, rather than identical across instances.

rows.subject: canonical model
rows.size_stated: one state variable and one parameter
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on the delayed-activation task across learning rates
rows.measure: normalized loss values; ability to learn
rows.value: Learning is no longer possible for α ≥ 9 * 10^-10; learning works with lower rates and more epochs, with best early progress near criticality.
rows.note: The paper reports loss and training behavior on its recurrent-inspired toy task, not classification error.
rows.check: The critical rate concerns entry into a flat no-learning zone, not the linearized stability threshold or curvature dynamics named in V5.

rows.subject: rank-one RNN
rows.operation_detail: Stochastic gradient descent on the delayed-activation task
rows.measure: loss and gradient norm during training
rows.value: Abrupt loss decrease and oscillatory behavior near a minimum; the network eventually escaped oscillations and decreased loss further.
rows.note: Authors report eventual progress and describe the learned loss minimum, but do not give a numerical final training classification error.
rows.check: Recovery from oscillations in a rank-one RNN does not establish recovery above the stability limit named in V5.

rows.subject: rank-one RNN
rows.operation_detail: Stochastic gradient descent on the delayed-activation task at a higher learning rate
rows.baseline: rank-one RNN trained with learning rate 0.003
rows.value: A saddle-node bifurcation occurred; the network remained stuck in a no-learning zone and could no longer recover, with a practically zero gradient.
rows.note: The text says the higher rate prevented learning altogether.
rows.check: Failure in a recurrent no-learning zone does not measure any listed version; no initial stability threshold is established.

rows.subject: rank-two RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on delayed cue discrimination task
rows.value: Training had abrupt loss transitions followed by oscillatory gradients; later loss decreased gradually as ghost timescales were fine-tuned, enabling appropriately timed output.
rows.uncertainty: s.e.m. values for output plots are described as negligible
rows.note: No numeric final classification error is reported.
rows.check: Rank-two recurrent working-memory learning falls outside the systems and comparisons specified by V1–V6.

rows.subject: rank-two RNN
rows.operation_detail: ADAM training on delayed match-to-sample task
rows.measure: loss and gradient dynamics; cue-comparison behavior
rows.value: Early training showed abrupt loss changes and later oscillatory gradients while trajectories failed to reliably separate match from mismatch; later training correctly distinguished and compared the cues.
rows.note: No numeric final classification error is reported.
rows.check: Rank-two recurrent cue-comparison learning does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: full-rank RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on delayed cue discrimination task
rows.measure: loss, gradient norm, and output accuracy
rows.value: Sharp loss decreases within the first ∼ 200 epochs with oscillatory gradients; reported accuracies include 0.39 at epoch 11, 0.87 at epoch 101, 0.86 at epoch 201, 0.96 at epoch 1001, and 0.98 at epoch 3001.
rows.note: The stated accuracy values are in the figure caption; the text describes later loss refinement and delayed outputs. This measures task accuracy, not classification training error on CIFAR.
rows.check: Reported accuracy is agreement across all times and trials after ternarizing outputs, not CIFAR training classification accuracy.

rows.subject: full-rank RNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on delayed match-to-sample task
rows.measure: loss, gradient norm, and output accuracy
rows.value: Training shows abrupt loss transitions and oscillatory gradients; reported accuracies include 0.89 at epochs 1001 and 50001, and 1.00 at epoch 100001.
rows.note: The caption reports accuracy values, while the text reports eventual correctly timed match versus no-match response.
rows.check: Reported accuracy is agreement across all times and trials after binarizing outputs, not CIFAR training classification accuracy.

rows.subject: rank-one RNN
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over learning rates for delayed-activation training
rows.value: Rank-one RNNs show the qualitative pattern of a critical learning rate beyond which learning fails; lower rates lead to eventual convergence, while rates just below the threshold yield fastest early progress.
rows.uncertainty: means and standard errors over ten random seeds
rows.note: No exact threshold value is stated in the accompanying text.
rows.check: The learning-rate sweep does not establish the stability-limit, loss-rise, or curvature conditions of V5.

rows.subject: full-rank RNN
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over learning rates for delayed-activation training
rows.value: Critical learning rate increased by nearly two orders of magnitude; rates near this value became optimal for sustained training.
rows.uncertainty: means and standard errors over ten random seeds
rows.note: The paper reports improved stability relative to rank one, while full-rank networks still exhibit a critical rate.
rows.check: Higher critical learning rates with full-rank recurrence do not measure V5's stability-relative recovery.

rows.subject: RNNs with varying ranks (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 30, 50, 100)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over number of trainable ranks for delayed-activation training
rows.value: Increasing trainable ranks shortened learning and led to milder and sustained loss decreases.
rows.uncertainty: each line corresponds to a run with a different seed
rows.note: The text says increasing ranks consistently resulted in learning with fewer epoch; exact per-rank values are figure-only.
rows.check: Trainable recurrent rank is not student width in V2. The authors also acknowledge possible changes in effective initialization across rank conditions.

rows.subject: RNNs with varying ranks (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 30, 50, 100)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over number of trainable ranks at a high learning rate
rows.value: Few RNNs that could train without entering a no-learning zone had higher ranks (here, K ≥ 10); higher-rank RNNs were substantially less likely to become trapped, particularly at larger learning rates, but did not fully eliminate instability.
rows.uncertainty: each line corresponds to a run with a different seed
rows.note: The text explicitly says full-rank networks still entered and often remained in no-learning zones.
rows.check: Rank-dependent avoidance of no-learning zones does not test spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks.

rows.subject: full-rank RNNs performing DMTS
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over learning rates, with each run trained for 20,000 epochs
rows.measure: loss and Frobenius norm of recurrent weight gradients averaged over training
rows.value: A critical learning rate is observed beyond which learning failed; at high rates, gradients averaged over the full training window remained small, indicating no-learning zones.
rows.uncertainty: each dot represents a run with a different seed; values averaged over all epochs
rows.check: Loss and gradient norms do not establish curvature or an initial linearized stability threshold.

rows.subject: full-rank RNNs performing DCD
rows.operation_detail: Sweep over learning rates, with each run trained for 20,000 epochs
rows.measure: loss and Frobenius norm of recurrent weight gradients averaged over training
rows.value: The DCD experiment qualitatively agreed with the DMTS findings, including critical learning rates and no-learning zones.
rows.note: The paper describes qualitative agreement and does not state an exact threshold.
rows.check: Recurrent learning failures across learning rates do not establish the stability-relative behavior specified by V5.

rows.subject: canonical model
rows.size_stated: one state variable and one parameter
rows.operation_detail: Measure loss gradients as a function of r at different output confidence levels
rows.measure: absolute gradient magnitude and training accuracy
rows.value: For infinite confidence, gradient is exactly zero for r < r*/4; excessively low confidence leads to incorrect outputs, with an optimal confidence level around c ≈ 0.1.
rows.note: The confidence sweep is a toy delayed-activation result, not a classification benchmark.
rows.check: Output-confidence effects do not measure any listed version. Figure 8A plots gradient magnitude; the optimal-confidence and incorrect-output statements are qualitative, not a plotted training-accuracy sweep.

rows.subject: 48 rank-one RNNs in no-learning zones
rows.operation_detail: Lower output confidence after training and recovery intervention

conditions.value: training accuracy of ≤ 0.5 for the last 50 epochs

rows.baseline: Before confidence reduction, 48 of 100 RNNs entered the no-learning zone.
rows.value: Lowering confidence allowed the RNNs to recover and relearn the task.
rows.note: The intervention changes confidence after the networks are stuck; it is not evidence about the model's unaided training outcome.
rows.check: Confidence reduction is an intervention outside all listed versions. The 48 networks are selected for failure; this row should distinguish that selected recovery cohort from the initial 100-network sample.

rows.subject: full-rank RNNs performing DCD
rows.operation_detail: Manually lower and fix output confidence at epoch 10,000

conditions.value: trainable in both cases during first 10,000 epochs

rows.value: After lowering and fixing confidence, output accuracy increased compared to baseline, in some cases reaching perfect performance; excessively low confidence prevented sustained learning.
rows.note: This is a post-training intervention on confidence; text does not give precise accuracy values.
rows.check: Baseline is continued learnable confidence, not a fixed-confidence condition. Confidence is trainable in all groups until epoch 10,000, when intervention groups receive fixed values. This intervention does not measure any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
